newsitem.title: GERMANY: Schwarz Pharma eyes 6 to 8 pct sales growth in 97.
newsitem.headline: Schwarz Pharma eyes 6 to 8 pct sales growth in 97.

text.p: German drugs group Schwarz Pharma AG, forecasting a 15 percent rise in 1996 sales, on Wednesday said sales will grow between six and eight percent next year while profits will rise more strongly.
The family-owned drugs group said nine month sales increased by 22.7 percent to 885.7 million marks, with foreign sales rising 34 percent and domestic sales rising 13.4 percent.

"For the business year 1997, the board forecasts a six to eight percent rise in sales as well as an overproportional rise in profits," Schwarz Pharma said in a mandatory statement, one day before a scheduled news conference.
Pre-tax profits in the first nine months of the year totalled 138.7 million marks with profits from ordinary activities totalling 142.8 million marks.
The company gave no comparison figures for the nine months, but said full year 1995 pre-tax profit totalled 174.5 million marks with profits from ordinary activities standing at 184.7 million marks.

For the full year 1996, Schwarz Pharma, a market favourite since listing its shares in 1995, forecast a 15 percent rise in sales and profits, with sales totalling 1.18 billion marks and the DVFA results standing at 96.9 million marks.
Broken down, Schwarz Pharma said its earnings per share, calculated according to the German DVFA method, will be 4.30 marks, marking a 15 percent rise from last year's result.
In light of strong developments, the group said it will raise its dividend by 20 percent to 1.50 marks per share, nominally valued at five marks.
Details about business developments will be provided on Thursday.
